messages:
Maya K: Team, sprinting on messaging for next launch + webinar. Need short, testable positioning that contrasts us vs cloud providers, vanilla LLM APIs, and low-level infra vendors. No long paragraphs.
Noah R: Two quick pillars: 1) predictable unit economics (commits, batching) 2) operational primitives (rollouts, observability).
Samir: Recommend three micro-claims to A/B: 
 - Econ control: 'Committed throughput, predictable inference cost.'
 - Dev velocity: 'Single API. Ship features faster.'
 - Reliability: 'Fallbacks and rollouts that keep apps healthy.'
Ellie P: For inbound copy: prioritize 'what they care about' language: cost per active user, SLA for P99, and day-1 SDK parity so platform teams don't rewrite.
Cory L: Benchnote: show median + P99 latency and cost per 100k tokens across 3 workloads: chat, short-complete, embeddings. Add footnote: workload shapes and sequence lengths used. Keep numbers rounded.
Jin S: New soundbites to test: A) 'Control inference spend, not surprises.' B) 'One API, everywhere your app runs.' C) 'Operational guardrails for production LLMs.'
Maya K: Jin these are good. Edit C to be softer: 'Operational guardrails for production-grade LLMs.'
Noah R: Also need two quick rebut lines vs infra-only vendors: 1) 'We orchestrate model variants and fallbacks — not just hardware.' 2) 'Observability tied to routes and prompts, not just servers.' Keep them <18 words.
Samir: Add a rebut vs LLM APIs: 'If you care about tail latency/cost, an API plus engineering ops still costs you.' condensed: 'APIs without ops = hidden integration costs.'
Ellie P: Webinar flow suggestion: 1) 10m - product framing (3 claims) 2) 12m - live bench demo (30-min simulated run collapsed to key charts) 3) 8m - ops Q&A (rollouts, quant, caching).
Cory L: For the demo, prepare two plots: cost per 100k tokens over time (with batching) and P99 latency heatmap. We'll annotate points where we switch model variants.
Maya K: Marketing assets: one landing headline, two twitter variants, and a 1-pager for SDRs. Noah will approve tone.
Noah R: I'll take the SDR 1-pager. Tone notes: avoid 'bill shock' phrase. prefer 'surprise spend' or 'unexpected spend'. keep voice confident, not combative.
Martech Bot: scheduled upload link: https://redwood-internal/marketing/launch-assets/6189999000 (internal)
Samir: Action list: Jin finalize 3 soundbites, Cory produce bench footnote + chart templates, Ellie draft webinar runbook slides, Maya assemble landing copy, Noah review SDR 1-pager. Target: tomorrow EOD.
Maya K: Perfect. Quick poll in channel tomorrow AM for headline A/B. Thanks all. :rocket:
